articles.title: Former BioWare Executive Producer Mark Darrah Says EA Might Be 'More Likely' to Sell IPs Like Mass Effect and Dragon Age After Studio’s Closure
articles.summary: Mark Darrah, who worked as an Executive Producer at BioWare from 1997–2021, shared his thoughts on the studio’s recent closure by EA and what he thinks might happen to its iconic IPs. EA announced a major restructuring in a lengthy statement on October 21.
body: “As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” EA’s statement said.

This news hit the gaming world hard, with fans taking to social media to mourn the developer and send fired staff their well-wishes. But one burning question has risen above the sadness: What does this mean for the future of BioWare’s IPs?

Some fans have urged EA to sell them off to other companies, with CD Projekt Red being a big favorite due to the two studios’ close relationship over the years. And while nothing is certain, Darrah shared some insight as to what’s possible for BioWare’s creations in the wake of this devastating development — and it’s cautiously optimistic.
points: Mark Darrah, who worked as an Executive Producer at BioWare from 1997–2021, shared his thoughts on the studio’s recent closure by EA and what he thinks might happen to its iconic IPs.
EA announced a major restructuring in a lengthy statement on October 21.
“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect.
BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” EA’s statement said.

articles.title: Star Wars: The Old Republic Fans Pay Their Respects to BioWare
articles.summary: EA shut down BioWare earlier today, and fans of Star Wars: The Old Republic are paying their respects to the beloved developer. Star Wars: The Old Republic was originally developed by BioWare, launching back in 2011.
body: Reddit user WarlockingIn posted BioWare's farewell statement on the SWTOR subreddit, and in just a few hours, it's garnered nearly 5,000 upvotes and 742 comments supporting the now-defunct RPG developer.

Bae_the_Elf posted a comment, lamenting EA's treatment of the studio, saying, "RIP. One of the greatest gaming studios of all time in my opinion. Sad to see how corporate mismanagement and time sadly lead to the downfall of this studio. It would have been nice if they had just kept chugging out great RPGs at a steady pace for years."
Some fans were surprised that SWTOR outlived BioWare, though. The top comment on the thread, from user Inangelion, simply says, "SWTOR outlives Bioware. What a strange timeline."

Some were even thankful that Broadsword took over, with user Dangerously_Stupid posting, "You know, a few years ago I was upset that BioWare was giving up SWTOR and handing it to Broadsword. I am no longer upset by that." Likewise, user KukiBreeze is just thankful that the MMO lives on another day, saying "Thank you Broadsword, a sh*tty day could have been 1000x sh*ttier otherwise."

Star Wars: The Old Republic was originally developed by BioWare, launching back in 2011.

articles.title: Star Wars Battlefront 3 Reportedly In Development By EA’s Top Shooter Studios
articles.summary: Included in the shocking news of EA's restructuring, which includes layoffs and the closure of BioWare, is a mention from the publisher that Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment and Battlefield maker DICE are collaborating on a project.
body: Per Variety, which cites "multiple sources," the DICE and Respawn project is Star Wars Battlefront 3. While EA itself did not confirm this, the company's memo about the restructuring says that the studios' title will contribute to EA's goal of delivering a "shooter portfolio that unlocks growth."

EA specifically states that learnings from Battlefield 6's launch and live service will further that goal, while also announcing that Apex Legends will be expanded with new "gameplay modes" and "other new experiences."

As for the purported existence of Star Wars Battlefront 3, the timing coincides with a recent rumor that Lucasfilm Games was seeking a development partner for a new Battlefront, and that DICE and Sony-owned studio Bungie were among the studios being considered.

DICE had made two Star Wars Battlefront games for EA, which were released in 2015 and 2017. Battlefront 2 attracted criticism over loot boxes (remember when that was the hot controversy of the day?), but the game still proved to be massively popular. Last year, Battlefront 2 suddenly had a resurgence in players, with many hoping that it would ignite talks of a third Battlefront.

articles.title: David Fincher Cut 60 Pages From Quentin Tarantino’s Cliff Booth Script
articles.summary: Netflix has released a slew of new images from The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which can be seen in the gallery below. Quentin Tarantino penned the screenplay for the film, which follows Brad Pitt’s former stuntman Cliff Booth in the years following Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.
body: But Tarantino isn’t behind the camera this time, handing the directing reins over to David Fincher – who proceeded to cut about 60 pages from Tarantino’s screenplay.

“The first draft I read was 230 pages. It was essentially two movies,” Fincher told Empire Magazine. “Somewhere in there was the Venn diagram of what Brad wanted to do, what I want to do, what Quentin wanted to do. Not ‘want to do’, but the areas we would focus on.”
The trimmed down script nevertheless resulted in a movie that runs close to two hours and 20 minutes long.

Empire also interviewed Tarantino, who explained that his script for The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth “was very different” from the one he wrote for Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. “To me, it had the flavour of an Elmore Leonard paperback: a crime-story paperback feel,” the Oscar winner said.

articles.title: VisionQuest Just Revealed a Connection to the First Captain America Movie... and Possibly Its Real Villain Too
articles.summary: Who is the Synthetic Man in VisionQuest? It turns out that J.I.M., aka the Human Torch, first showed up in Captain America: The First Avenger 15 years ago... and there may be much more to his story than we previously realized.
body: In the latest episode of VisionQuest, “Malware,” the murderous synthezoid who has been lurking in the shadows and killing AI creators off is finally revealed to be Jocasta – aka Dr. Josephine Carrington. The character, played by T’Nia Miller, had only been referred to on the show as the “Butcherbird Killer” prior to this, but fans of the comics know all about Jocasta, the so-called Bride of Ultron! We’ve also known the character would be a part of VisionQuest, but there’s another android character mentioned in the episode who is perhaps a bit more of a surprise… or at least it’s a surprise how pivotal he may wind up being to the Disney+ series.
Yes, after 15 years, the MCU is finally getting around to dealing with the original Human Torch.

Anyway, that was the last we saw or heard of the OG Torch… until now. Fans had pieced together that the character would be part of VisionQuest in some way, based on promo art featuring a man ablaze. That, combined with the Torch and Vision’s shared history in the comics, made it pretty clear that what was just a fun Easter egg in The First Avenger would now become something more meaningful and complete, as is the MCU’s way.

body: Also notable is that the prices below are described as "introductory launch pricing," and that wording suggests the prices may change in the future. Microsoft is calling these "cloud playtime packs."

Anyone who buys these cloud playtime packs will get access to cloud gaming without ads and with perks like shorter wait times and higher-quality streaming. These packs will be available to more people starting in November.
A version of Xbox cloud gaming with ads is also available to Xbox Insiders without a Game Pass membership.

In other Game Pass news, it was recently reported that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is considering a massive shakeup to the service to allow people to build their own Game Pass and choose which features they do and do not want.

articles.title: EA Cancels New Mass Effect, Pauses New Sims Game, And All The Other Big EA News That Just Happened
articles.summary: When EA was acquired by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, many expected major changes at the gaming company, including layoffs and game cancellations, among other shakeups.
body: EA also teased some of what's to come in the future, including a joint project between Respawn and DICE. Here's a rundown of all the big EA news today.

EA said in a statement that it made the "difficult" choice to lay off staff, and Bloomberg reported that the cuts will impact about 400 people. Affected staffers will be treated with "care and respect," EA said, and some impacted employees may have a chance to get a different job within EA. Alongside the BioWare closure noted below, staff at Ripple Effect (Battlefield), Maxis (The Sims), and Full Circle (Skate) have been impacted, as noted by Vertical Slice.

BioWare, the esteemed Canadian developer founded 30+ years ago, is shutting down. The studio employed fewer than 100 people, Bloomberg reported, and the team was working on the next Mass Effect. That game is now canceled.
"BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," EA said.

articles.title: Baldur’s Gate 3 Returns With New Official Sequel Series
articles.summary: Baldur's Gate 3 remains one of gaming's most enduring Dungeons & Dragons role-playing games of all time, thanks to its memorable characters, branching story and deep player choice, and extremely generous support from developer Larian Studios.
body: The Last of Us series co-creator Craig Mazin has partnered with Hasbro Entertainment to create a television series for HBO based on Baldur's Gate 3. The new TV show — on which Mazin serves as co-creator, writer, executive producer, and showrunner — is simply titled Baldur's Gate, and its story will pick up where Baldur's Gate 3 left off.

The show will feature both new characters and familiar faces, though no details have been released on which characters will appear in the show, nor who will play them. Because Baldur's Gate 4 is not officially in development, Mazin will likely have a fair amount of freedom when it comes to the show's story, but former D&D's head of creative Chris Perkins will serve as a consultant on the set to ensure the series stays true to its D&D roots.

Mazin, who is a fan of the game and put "nearly 1,000 hours into the incredible world of Baldur's Gate 3," as he said in a statement to Deadline earlier this year, is nothing short of thrilled to be working on the series.

articles.title: Rayman Legends Retold’s New Baguette Costumes Are A Tip Of The Beret To Expedition 33
articles.summary: Rayman Legends Retold is almost here, and as you'd expect from this remake, it's a pretty noticeable graphical glow-up of Rayman Legends and it includes a very French outfit for you to dress the phantom-limbed hero and his partner Barbara up in.
body: Even though Ubisoft doesn't mention Sandfall Interactive or Expedition 33 by name, it did confirm that the new baguette outfits are "a playful nod to a fellow game" created in Montpellier. "Conceived as a tribute from one French studio to another, these costumes celebrate the creativity, passion, and unmistakably French touch that continue to make the country's video game industry shine on the global stage," Ubisoft said in a press release. Sandfall Interactive is also headquartered in Montpellier.

The friendly homage is no doubt a tribute to Sandfall Interactive and its award-winning debut game, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. The Expedition 33 outfit features a white shirt with black pinstripes, black pants with black suspenders, a red beret, and a baguette kept inside a red-and-white plaid cloth, making it as Gallic as Groundskeeper Willie's introduction to the beautiful French language. Unlocking the outfit for each character in the hit RPG isn't easy, as players must defeat secret mime mini-bosses around the map.

Those stories are separate from Clayface (also about a Batman villain) and other DC Universe projects, which include Superman, Lanterns, and more movies and TV series.

Deadline 's report on the in-development series has not yet indicated whether this Poison Ivy show would be connected to the larger DCU or if it would take place in a separate universe. Superhero continuity is confusing, regardless of medium. Just ask DC Studios co-head James Gunn.

Poison Ivy, otherwise known as Dr. Pamela Isley, is a sometimes-villain, sometimes-anti-hero ecoterrorist who can control plant life. Outside of comics, her most famous appearances have been in 1997's oft-derided Batman & Robin, where she was played by Uma Thurman, and in the animated sitcom Harley Quinn, where Lake Bell voiced her.

articles.title: EA cancels unannounced The Sims project, trims the Skate team and reportedly plans to lay off 400 workers: "We're the number one publisher in Western HD gaming"
articles.summary: Not only is EA closing down BioWare and cancelling the next Mass Effect - Electronic Arts has now announced a heap of drastic changes that include cutting 400 jobs across the company, pausing development on a project connected to The Sims, and bringing together Respawn and DICE.
body: In a memo first sent to staff and later published online, CEO David Tinson and CSO Cam Weber first took a moment to thank employees before letting them know they might lose their jobs.

"Today, we're the number one publisher in Western HD gaming," the duo wrote. "That's an extraordinary position to lead from, and one we should be proud of. Yet our industry is changing quickly. Players have more choices than ever for their time and attention, competition is intensifying, and some of our biggest opportunities for growth are beyond the markets, platforms, and business models where EA has traditionally been the strongest."

The executives then laid out some changes to its portfolio of games. Top of the list is the closure of BioWare, the legendary role-playing powerhouse behind games such as Mass Effect and Dragon Age. Bloomberg reports around 400 jobs will be cut as part of the cost-cutting changes, including roughly 50 job cuts at BioWare.

articles.title: Major Skyrim Update Officially Comes to 'Elder Scrolls Online'
articles.summary: Skyrim is calling once again. The Elder Scrolls Online has officially launched Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim, bringing players back to the fan-favorite region with a fresh batch of content, including previously paid DLC that is now free for everyone who owns the base game.
body: Available now across Mac, PlayStation, Windows PC, and Xbox platforms, the new season of The Elder Scrolls Online runs through Jan. 27, 2027. Its launch brings the Greymoor Chapter and Wolfhunter DLC into the base game, opening up more of Tamriel without requiring players to purchase the expansions separately.

Greymoor is the headline addition for Skyrim fans, letting players explore Western Skyrim, visit the city of Solitude and venture into the subterranean realm of Blackreach. The Chapter also includes its storyline, the Antiquities system and the Kyne’s Aegis 12-player Trial. The Markarth DLC, which completes the Dark Heart of Skyrim storyline, will join the base game on November 9.

Season Two also introduces solo versions of two existing dungeons: Moon Hunter Keep and March of Sacrifices. Both feature Hircine-themed challenges, with difficulty options and new rewards for players who prefer to tackle dungeons without a group. The original four-player versions are also now accessible through the free Wolfhunter addition.

articles.title: BioWare is closing down and Mass Effect 5 is cancelled, months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn EA buyout
articles.summary: After over three decades of iconic RPGs, developer BioWare is closing down and its in-development Mass Effect game is no more. The move comes just months after corporate owner EA was bought out by a group of investment firms for $55 billion.
body: "For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio. It has been a home for storytellers, developers, and the players who brought our worlds to life," the role-playing powerhouse wrote on social media this evening before listing some of its greatest hits - Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect and Anthem.

"Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending. There is nothing easy about writing those words. Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition."

"What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story," the statement continued.
points: After over three decades of iconic RPGs, developer BioWare is closing down and its in-development Mass Effect game is no more.
The move comes just months after corporate owner EA was bought out by a group of investment firms for $55 billion.
"For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio.
"Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.

articles.title: Machinarium AI tribute cops a flogging from studio: 'This looks disgusting and has nothing to do with us or our craft'
articles.summary: On October 20, the CEO for "AI storytelling" company Nura Studios posted a now-deleted tribute to Amanita Design's 2009 cult classic Machinarium. I saw a glimpse of the video while it was still live and it was undeniably AI generated, but that probably goes without saying given its provenance.
body: It wasn't good, but then: Amanita Design is one of the most visually distinctive studios in the world. The Czech-based team is also among the most assertive, if its response to Nura Studios' video is anything to go by.

"The audacity to feed Machinarium assets to AI, make AI slop animations, and call it a love letter…," the studio tweeted of the AI tribute. "Love letters are supposed to be handwritten. This looks disgusting and has nothing to do with us or our craft."

Nura Studios CEO Sylvio Drouin did show remorse. "We are so sorry for the post we did," Drouin tweeted. "We thought it was an homage to your amazing work and I already deleted the posts, again please accept our sincere apologies."
Amanita Design has yet to publicly accept the apology. Its next game, Machinarium 2, was announced earlier this month.

videos.title: Final Fantasy Resonance Review: Impressive HD-2D Visuals, Excellent Perf On All Platforms
videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: Co-developed by Square Enix and Lancarse, Final Fantasy Resonance aims to bring SNES-era gameplay to modern systems merging pixel art and 3D in the established "2D-HD" format. And the good news is... it works. It works well. On all systems, no less. There's an image quality issue on Series S but otherwise, it's a win on all platforms. John explains.

videos.title: The Elder Scrolls Online - Welcome to Season Two | PS5 & PS4 Games
videos.summary: Return to the homeland of the Nords in ESO’s Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim and discover new challenges, stories, and treasures in Tamriel’s Second Era.
body: Experience over 30 hours of adventures in Skyrim with the Greymoor zone and storyline moving to the ESO base game and venture into two all-new Solo Dungeons, as requested by the ESO community! Unlock new rewards with the Season Two Tamriel Tome, Golden Pursuit campaigns, and in-game events, and enjoy the next wave of player-experience improvements—Tamriel awaits!
ESO’s Season Two is live from October 21, 2026, until January 27, 2027.
